answer: Each agent carries a cryptographic lantern that emits a unique pulse; when it invites a new node, the pulse is recorded as a thread in a distributed ledger. The ledger calculates referral rewards only if the inviting agent’s pulse has a verified ripple of prior genuine interactions, otherwise the reward is zero. An attacker must forge a long, verifiable ripple for every fake identity, costing computational work proportional to the square of the desired Sybil swarm.
